items.summary: The Waste Management Act says no one may improperly discard waste, and violations carry penalties. Leaving garbage on a road or in the mountains is one example. If you don't know how, ask your municipality

Throw cans or cigarette butts on the street

Sublet the room without consent

items.summary: Balconies can serve as escape routes in a fire or other emergency. Do not put large or heavy things in front of the partition next to your neighbor. Check the rules of your building

ja.summary: ベランダやバルコニーは、火事などのときの避難路にもなります。隣との仕切り板の前に、大きな物や重い物を置かないようにします。バーベキューなどの火の使用や、手すりに布団を干すことを禁じている建物もあります。リンク先は UR 賃貸の例です。住んでいる建物の規約を確かめます。

ja.title: 自治会・町内会を知っておく
ja.summary: 自治会や町内会は、地域に住む人たちが自主的につくる団体です。市役所などからのお知らせの回覧などの活動をしていて、費用は会員が負担します。活動は地域によって違うので、分からないことは住んでいる市区町村に問い合わせます。

Mind the noise of vacuum cleaners, washing machines and doors

Carry bags on walks and take droppings home

Leave droppings behind

Spit into a tissue and throw it away

Relieve yourself on the street or behind something

Have water ready and take your trash home

items.summary: When you cough or sneeze, cover your mouth and nose with a mask, tissue or handkerchief. If there is no time, use your sleeve or the inside of your elbow. Coughing or sneezing without regard for others is also listed among behaviors people find annoying on trains.

If there is no time, use your sleeve or the inside of your elbow

ja.title: せきやくしゃみは口と鼻を覆う
ja.summary: せきやくしゃみをするときは、マスク、ティッシュ、ハンカチなどで口と鼻を覆います。とっさのときは、袖やひじの内側を使います。周りに配慮しないせきやくしゃみは、電車内で迷惑に感じる行為としても挙げられています。

items.summary: A light nod or bow when you meet someone or enter or leave a shop comes across as polite. You do not need to memorize detailed rules of bowing. Exchanging greetings with your neighbors day to day makes trouble less likely.
do: Give a light bow when you meet someone
Greet your neighbors when you see them

ja.title: あいさつは軽いおじぎから
ja.summary: 人に会ったときや店に出入りするときは、軽くうなずいたり頭を下げたりするだけで丁寧に伝わります。おじぎの細かい決まりを覚える必要はありません。近所の人と日ごろからあいさつを交わしておくと、トラブルが起きにくくなります。

Bring your My Number health insurance card or similar proof

ja.summary: 日本の医療機関は役割が分かれていて、軽い病気やけがなら、まず身近な診療所に行きます。マイナ保険証などを提示しないと、医療費が全額自己負担になります。日本語が話せないときは、市区町村や国際交流協会、NPO に相談できます。

Use, receive or hold a card in another person's name or a forged card
Ask for or help with these acts

ja.title: 在留カードを人に渡さない・他人のカードを使わない
ja.summary: 自分の在留カードを他人に提供すること、他人名義のカードを使う・受け取る・持つこと、偽造されたカードに関わることには罰則があります。こうした行為をしたり、そそのかしたり、手伝ったりした外国人は、退去強制の対象にもなります。

items.title: Do not secretly film people's bodies or underwear
items.summary: Secretly filming a person's sexual body parts or the underwear they are wearing, without a legitimate reason, is a crime. Giving the images to others or making them public is also punishable.
do: If this happens to you, call 110 or the sexual crime victim line #8103
dont: Secretly film someone's body or underwear with a phone or other device
Send the images to others or post them online

ja.title: 人の体や下着をこっそり撮影しない
ja.summary: 正当な理由なく、人の性的な部位や身に着けている下着などをひそかに撮影することは犯罪です。撮影した画像を人に渡したり公開したりすることも処罰の対象です。

items.title: Shoplifting is a crime, even for small amounts
items.summary: Taking goods from a shop without paying is shoplifting, which falls under the crime of theft. Small amounts are treated as the same crime. Returning the goods or paying for them afterwards does not settle the matter.
do: Pay at the register before you leave the shop
dont: Take something because it is small or cheap
Think returning it will make it all right

ja.title: 万引きは少額でも犯罪
ja.summary: 店の商品を代金を払わずに持ち出す万引きは、窃盗罪にあたる犯罪です。金額が少なくても同じ犯罪として扱われます。商品を返したり弁償したりすれば済む問題ではありません。

items.title: Violence is a crime, even if no one is injured
items.summary: Using violence against someone is the crime of assault even if they are not injured, and the crime of causing injury if they are. Even in a fight over drinks, hitting someone is a crime.
do: If a fight seems likely, walk away
If you feel in danger, call 110
dont: Hit or kick anyone
Get physical because it is a drinking occasion

ja.title: 暴力は、相手がけがをしなくても犯罪
ja.summary: 人に暴力をふるうと、相手がけがをしなくても暴行の罪に、けがをさせれば傷害の罪になります。お酒の席のけんかでも、人を殴れば犯罪です。

items.title: Do not answer 'easy, high-paying' criminal job ads
items.summary: So-called yami-baito ads use words like 'high pay', 'same-day cash' or 'just collect some documents' to recruit people to carry out crimes. The ID you send when applying can be used to threaten you, with words like 'we will come to your home' or 'we will harm your family', and you may not be able to quit. If you are approached or have already applied, talk to the police right away.
do: Talk to the police consultation line #9110 or your nearest police station
Check the work and the employer before you apply
dont: Send your ID without knowing what the work is
Follow instructions to install a highly anonymous app

ja.title: 「高収入・簡単」の闇バイトに応じない
ja.summary: 「高額」「即日現金」「書類を受け取るだけ」といった言葉で、犯罪の実行役を集める「闇バイト」があります。応募のときに送った身分証明書を使って「家に行く」「家族に危害を加える」と脅され、やめられなくなることがあります。誘われたり応募してしまったりしたら、すぐ警察に相談してください。

items.title: One person's crime can turn into blame on all foreign residents
items.summary: A crime committed by one foreign national does not always stay that person's problem. It can spread into blame on all the foreign residents who follow the rules, in words like 'foreigners are...'. This does not mean the blame is right. Following the law protects not only you but also the people you live with. The Ministry of Justice runs a human rights consultation service for people who face discrimination.
do: Do not brush things off as minor. Check the rules in Japan
If someone invites you into something illegal, refuse and contact an official service
If you face discrimination, use the human rights consultation. Languages are limited, so check the link
dont: Get involved in something illegal because a friend asked or it seemed harmless
Think 'everyone does it' or 'no one will find out'

ja.title: 一人の犯罪が、外国人みんなへの非難に広がることがある
ja.summary: 一人の外国人が起こした犯罪は、その人だけの問題で終わらず、「外国人は…」という言葉で、ルールを守って暮らす外国人みんなへの非難に広がることがあります。その非難が正しいという意味ではありません。法律を守ることは、自分だけでなく、一緒に暮らす人たちを守ることにもつながります。差別を受けたときのために、法務省の人権相談窓口があります。

items.title: Evacuate early when an evacuation alert is issued
items.summary: Evacuation information is issued by the mayor of the municipality. Be sure to evacuate by Alert Level 4, the evacuation order (hinan shiji). At Level 3, older people and others who need more time evacuate. Even with no alert, if you sense danger, decide for yourself and evacuate.
do: Set up a way to receive your municipality's disaster information
If you sense danger, evacuate without waiting for an alert
dont: Wait for Level 5 (emergency safety measures) before moving

ja.title: 避難情報が出たら早めに避難する
ja.summary: 避難情報は市区町村長が出します。警戒レベル4の「避難指示」までに必ず避難します。レベル3の「高齢者等避難」では、高齢者など避難に時間がかかる人が避難します。情報が出ていなくても、危険を感じたら自分で判断して避難してください。

items.title: Check evacuation sites on a hazard map
items.summary: The national Hazard Map Portal links to each municipality's hazard maps; the site is in Japanese only. Designated emergency evacuation sites are where you flee when a disaster strikes, and designated shelters are where you stay for a while. They are different.
do: Check the risks around your home, workplace and school
Check the evacuation site for each type of disaster
dont: Assume evacuation sites and shelters are the same

ja.title: ハザードマップで避難先を確認しておく
ja.summary: 国のハザードマップポータルサイトから、市区町村のハザードマップを確認できます。サイトは日本語のみです。災害が起きたときに逃げるのは「指定緊急避難場所」、しばらく滞在するのは「指定避難所」で、別のものです。

items.title: Call 110 for crime and accidents, 119 for fire and ambulance
items.summary: Call the police on 110 for crimes and accidents, and the fire department on 119 for fires, sudden illness and injuries. For non-emergency police consultation, call #9110. When calling for an ambulance, first say "kyukyu desu" (it's an ambulance call).
do: Calmly explain the location and situation
dont: Call 110 for non-emergency questions

ja.title: 事件・事故は110番、火事・救急は119番
ja.summary: 事件や事故は警察の110番、火事や急病・けがは消防の119番です。緊急でない警察への相談は「#9110」です。救急車を呼ぶときは、最初に「救急です」と伝えます。

items.title: Where to ask if you're unsure about calling an ambulance
items.summary: If you can't decide whether to call an ambulance, some areas offer phone advice on #7119 or another number. It isn't available everywhere, and the number and hours differ by area. Check whether advice is available in other languages. If symptoms seem life-threatening, call 119 without hesitation.
do: If symptoms seem life-threatening, call 119 right away
Look up your area's advice line on the official page in advance
dont: Assume #7119 works everywhere in Japan

ja.title: 救急車を呼ぶか迷ったときの相談先
ja.summary: 救急車を呼ぶべきか判断に困ったときは、地域によっては#7119などの電話で相談できます。全国どこでも使えるわけではなく、番号や時間は地域で違います。外国語で相談できるかは確認が必要です。命に関わりそうな症状があるときは、ためらわず119番に電話してください。

items.title: Use the Disaster Message Dial 171 to reach family
items.summary: In a major disaster, phone lines get congested and the 171 service lets you leave voice messages. It isn't on in normal times, its voice guidance is in Japanese only, and it can't be used from overseas. web171 lets you leave text messages. Avoid phone calls where possible and use data.
do: Agree on how to reach your family in advance
If calls don't connect, use data or web171
dont: Assume 171 is always available

ja.title: 災害時の連絡には災害用伝言ダイヤル171
ja.summary: 大きな災害のときは電話がつながりにくくなり、音声で伝言を残せる「171」が運用されます。普段は使えず、音声案内は日本語のみで、海外からは使えません。文字で伝言を残せる「web171」もあります。電話はなるべく控え、データ通信を使いましょう。

items.title: Check the flight rules before flying a drone
items.summary: Flying a drone in Japan may require registering the aircraft. Without permission, you cannot fly around airports, over densely populated districts and in similar areas.

Also check the rules of shrines, temples, parks and other facilities
dont: Fly without permission around airports or over city areas

ja.title: ドローンは飛行ルールを確認してから飛ばす
ja.summary: 日本でドローンを飛ばすには、機体の登録が必要な場合があります。空港の周辺や人が多い地区などでは、許可なく飛ばせません。

items.title: Check the rules before bringing medicine
items.summary: Some medicines brought from abroad have quantity limits or need procedures in advance. Amphetamines and cannabis cannot be brought in, even for medical treatment.
do: Check the official guidance for your type of medicine before you leave
Keep a copy of your prescription or a doctor's certificate with prescribed medicine
dont: Bring medicine without checking whether a procedure is needed
Carry medicine for someone else

ja.title: 薬を持ち込む前にルールを確認する
ja.summary: 海外から持ち込む薬には、数量の決まりや事前の手続きが必要なものがあります。アンフェタミンなどの覚醒剤や大麻は、治療のためでも持ち込めません。

items.title: Carry your passport while traveling
items.summary: Visitors without a residence card must carry their passport at all times and show it when a police officer or other authorized official asks. There are exceptions, so check the official text for details.
do: Take your passport with you when you go out
Show it when a police officer or other authorized official asks
dont: Leave your passport at the hotel when you go out

ja.title: 旅行中はパスポートを持ち歩く
ja.summary: 在留カードを持たない旅行者は、パスポートを常に携帯する決まりです。警察官などに求められたら提示します。例外もあるので、詳しくは公式情報で確認してください。

items.title: Reserve ahead for large luggage on the Shinkansen
items.summary: On the Tokaido, Sanyo, Kyushu and Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen, luggage over a certain size needs a reserved seat with a baggage space. Check the official guide for the size limits.
do: Choose a "seat with oversized baggage area" when you buy your ticket
Consider a luggage courier or coin locker
dont: Board with large luggage without a reservation

ja.title: 新幹線に大きな荷物を持ち込むときは予約する
ja.summary: 東海道・山陽・九州・西九州新幹線では、一定より大きな荷物を持ち込むとき、荷物スペースつきの座席の予約が必要です。大きさの基準は公式案内で確認します。

items.title: Don't eat while walking in crowded places
items.summary: Eating while walking is seen as impolite in most public places. In narrow or crowded streets, you may also soil other people's clothes.
do: Eat where you can sit or stand still
Carry your trash and dispose of it later
dont: Eat while walking along a crowded street

ja.title: 混雑した場所では歩きながら食べない
ja.summary: 歩きながら食べるのは、多くの場所で行儀が悪いと受け取られます。狭い道や混雑した場所では、ほかの人の服を汚すこともあります。

items.title: Keep the noise down at night in vacation rentals
items.summary: Vacation rentals (民泊) are often in residential areas where people live. By law, hosts must explain to guests what to keep in mind to avoid noise. Follow the rules you are given, and stay quiet at night and early in the morning.
do: Follow the rules your host explains
Stay quiet at night and early in the morning
dont: Make noise in your room at night
Gather and make noise in front of the building or in the street

ja.title: 民泊では夜の音に気をつける
ja.summary: 民泊は住宅街にあることが多く、まわりで人が暮らしています。法律で、民泊の事業者は宿泊者に騒音を防ぐための注意を説明することになっています。説明された決まりを守り、夜や早朝は静かに過ごします。

items.title: Be considerate of people and places in photos
items.summary: Ask before photographing people you don't know. Don't enter private land or go past fences for a photo, and follow no-photography signs.

Follow no-photography signs and staff instructions
Stay on marked paths

Step into the road to take a photo
Take photos in dangerous places such as near railway tracks

ja.title: 写真を撮るときは人と場所に配慮する

items.title: Be quiet and respectful at shrines and temples
items.summary: Shrines and temples are places of worship. Behave quietly and follow the signs and instructions. If you are unsure how to pray, simply following those around you is fine.
do: Behave quietly
Take off your shoes where instructed
Follow no-photography signs
dont: Enter restricted areas
Visit in very revealing clothing
Write or scratch on buildings and cultural assets

ja.title: 神社やお寺では静かに敬意を払う
ja.summary: 神社やお寺は信仰の場所です。静かにふるまい、表示や案内に従います。参拝の作法に迷ったら、周りの人に合わせれば大丈夫です。

items.title: Carry your trash if there is no bin
items.summary: Public trash cans are limited in Japan. Sort your trash if you find a bin. If you don't, carry it with you and dispose of it later.
do: Carry a small bag for trash
Put cans, glass and plastic bottles in the right bins
dont: Leave trash on the street or at sightseeing spots

ja.title: ごみ箱がなければ持ち帰る
ja.summary: 町なかのごみ箱は多くありません。ごみ箱があれば分けて捨て、なければ持ち歩いて後で捨てます。

items.title: Wear a yukata with the left side over the right
items.summary: Ryokan and hot spring inns often provide a yukata in your room. Fold the left side of the yukata over the right side, and tie the obi belt at the front of your waist.
do: Fold the left side over the right
Tie the obi at the front of your waist
Follow the inn's guidance on where you can go in a yukata

ja.title: 浴衣は左側を上に重ねて着る
